strengths: Clear motivation and elegant operator design: The paper addresses a timely limitation in foundation model feature upsampling, where recent methods have defaulted to quadratic-cost cross-attention. The proposed Local Attender offers a simple, parameter-efficient linear-time alternative based on fixed directional offsets that retains semantic stability without quadratic complexity.

Strong empirical results on predictive tasks: Across four standard semantic segmentation benchmarks (COCO-Stuff, VOC, ADE20K, Cityscapes) and monocular depth estimation, UPLiFT consistently outperforms recent cross-attention baselines (LoftUp, JAFAR, AnyUp) while being substantially faster.

Comprehensive scaling analysis: The authors provide detailed latency and memory scaling comparisons on multiple GPU architectures (A5000 and H100), demonstrating robust linear scaling up to tens of thousands of tokens where existing cross-attention baselines run out of memory.

Novel application to generative feature spaces: Extending feature upsampling to VAE latent spaces for diffusion upscaling and 4x image super-resolution is a compelling contribution, demonstrating competitive visual fidelity and significant latency advantages over Coupled Flow Matching (CFM).

Extensive ablations: The submission thoroughly explores training depth configurations, neighborhood topologies/sizes, encoder/decoder capacities, and directly compares the proposed Local Attender against Windowed Cross-Attention (NATTEN).
weaknesses: Trade-offs in generative distribution matching: In the image super-resolution experiments (Table 4), although UPLiFT achieves higher SSIM/PSNR, its FID scores on FacesHQ (5.20 vs. 1.36) and LHQ (5.29 vs. 2.27) lag noticeably behind CFM. While the authors note that CFM models are dataset-specific, this indicates that the deterministic/linear-combination nature of UPLiFT may struggle to match complex high-frequency distribution statistics compared to generative flow models.

Inflexibility to arbitrary scale factors: Unlike continuous coordinate-based or cross-attention upsamplers that can query arbitrary non-integer output resolutions directly, UPLiFT relies on discrete 2x iterative stages, requiring over-upsampling and bilinear downsampling when targeting non-power-of-two resolutions.

Missing empirical comparison with content-aware reassembly baselines: The Local Attender shares conceptual similarities with dynamic local aggregation methods such as CARAFE or SAPA (predicting local kernels from guidance features to reassemble low-res values). While cited in related work, an explicit empirical comparison or ablation against CARAFE would clarify how much gain comes from the specific multi-step formulation versus existing content-aware reassembly operators.

strengths: Well-motivated and efficient design: The proposed Local Attender sidesteps the quadratic time and memory scaling of standard QKV cross-attention while overcoming the semantic drift problems of prior iterative methods like LiFT, achieving strictly linear O(nT) complexity with respect to token count.

Strong and consistent empirical performance on predictive tasks: UPLiFT achieves state-of-the-art results across four standard semantic segmentation benchmarks (COCO-Stuff, Pascal VOC, ADE20K, Cityscapes) and competitive monocular depth estimation performance, while operating significantly faster than prior baselines (LoftUp, JAFAR, AnyUp).

Novel extension to generative latent spaces: The paper successfully validates feature upsampling on VAE latent representations for both text-to-image super-resolution (SD 1.5) and image super-resolution, showing that a feed-forward iterative upsampler can achieve competitive quality compared to computationally heavy Coupled Flow Matching models.

Comprehensive ablations and systems evaluation: The paper provides extensive analyses including neighborhood structure, training depth schedules, comparisons against Windowed Cross-Attention (NATTEN), backbone generalizations (DINOv3, ResNet, ConvNeXt), and detailed hardware benchmarking (A5000 and H100) detailing latency and GPU memory scaling.
weaknesses: Conceptual overlap with dynamic and content-aware filtering: The Local Attender uses a high-resolution guide feature to predict localized spatial weights via a 1x1 convolution and softmax to linearly resample values over a fixed neighborhood. This mechanism shares strong conceptual similarities with existing content-aware filtering techniques (e.g., CARAFE, PAC-Conv, dynamic filtering). Further discussion and direct empirical comparison clarifying these connections would strengthen the methodological positioning.

Inherent rigidity of iterative 2x scaling: Unlike continuous coordinate- or cross-attention-based upsamplers (e.g., JAFAR, LoftUp) that can directly query arbitrary resolutions, UPLiFT relies on iterative discrete 2x stages. For backbones with non-power-of-two patch sizes (such as DINOv2 with patch size 14), the model must over-upsample to 16x and then downsample to 14x, sacrificing some arbitrary-scale flexibility.

Ad-hoc modifications needed for generative tasks: Adapting the architecture to VAE latent upsampling requires noticeable manual tailoring, including scaling model parameters from 0.8M to 53.5M, adding post-attender refiner blocks, injecting noise channels, switching normalization schemes, and adding an inference-time heuristic color correction step.

Quality gap in generative perceptual metrics: While UPLiFT is much faster and more parameter-efficient than Coupled Flow Matching (CFM), there remains a noticeable gap in distribution-level generation metrics (e.g., FID of 5.20 vs. 1.36 on FacesHQ, and 5.29 vs. 2.27 on LHQ), indicating that deterministic linear feature pooling cannot fully replace generative diffusion/flow models in synthesizing realistic high-frequency generative details.

strengths: Clear motivation and well-executed design: The paper effectively revisits iterative feature upsampling, addressing the severe semantic drift observed in prior iterative methods (e.g., LiFT) via a lightweight Local Attender operator that constrains feature distributions through guided local linear pooling.

Efficiency and scalability: By eschewing standard QKV cross-attention and global operations, UPLiFT exhibits strictly linear time and memory complexity with respect to token counts. The optimized UPLiFT-Fast variant (leveraging fused Triton kernels and memory format alignment) demonstrates superior throughput and memory efficiency, scaling to high token counts (>14k tokens on A5000 and ~50k tokens on H100) where baseline cross-attention methods OOM.

Strong empirical performance on predictive tasks: Across four standard semantic segmentation benchmarks (COCO-Stuff, Pascal VOC, ADE20K, Cityscapes) and monocular depth estimation, UPLiFT consistently matches or outperforms prior upsampling methods (FeatUp, LiFT, JAFAR, LoftUp, AnyUp) while retaining lower latency. Generality is further demonstrated across DINOv2, DINOv3, and standard CNN backbones.

Comprehensive exploration of generative latent upsampling: Extending task-agnostic feature upsampling to VAE latents in Latent Diffusion models is an interesting direction. UPLiFT achieves competitive text-to-image FID and super-resolution results compared to Coupled Flow Matching (CFM) while requiring substantially fewer parameters, training samples, and inference time.

Thorough ablations: The paper provides extensive ablations analyzing multi-depth loss supervision, local neighborhood configurations, model capacity trade-offs, and head-to-head comparisons against Windowed Cross-Attention (NATTEN).
weaknesses: Inherent rigidity in target output resolutions: Unlike continuous coordinate/query-based cross-attention upsamplers (e.g., JAFAR, LoftUp) that can resample directly to arbitrary non-integer dimensions, UPLiFT relies on discrete $2\times$ convolutional stages. Handling patch sizes such as 14 requires over-upsampling to $16\times$ followed by downsampling, introducing an architectural constraint.

Architectural divergence between predictive and generative regimes: While the predictive model is lightweight (0.8M parameters), the generative latent upsampling task requires substantial architectural adaptations—scaling to ~53.5M parameters, adding noise injection channels, replacing BatchNorm with LayerNorm, and introducing a post-attender Refiner Block. This indicates that the core Local Attender formulation alone is insufficient to model complex generative latent distributions.

Generative perceptual quality trade-off: In the image super-resolution benchmarks (Table 4), while UPLiFT attains higher reconstruction metrics (SSIM/PSNR), CFM demonstrates significantly better perceptual distribution fidelity (e.g., FacesHQ FID of 1.36 vs. UPLiFT's 5.20; LHQ FID of 2.27 vs. 5.29), showing that direct regression/upsampling still lags behind iterative diffusion/flow-based generative modeling for fine texture synthesis.

Contextualization with content-aware dynamic filtering: The proposed Local Attender predicts localized blending weights from a guidance map and applies them to offset value features. This formulation is closely related to existing dynamic filtering mechanisms (e.g., CARAFE, Pixel-Adaptive Convolutions). Discussing and explicitly differentiating the Local Attender from these content-aware filtering techniques would clarify its conceptual novelty.

strengths: Clear motivation and problem setting: The paper convincingly identifies key bottlenecks in existing feature upsamplers—namely, the quadratic computational/memory scaling of recent cross-attention-based approaches (LoftUp, JAFAR, AnyUp) and the semantic drift problem in prior iterative methods (LiFT).

Effective and elegant Local Attender operator: By formulating local attentional pooling via fixed directional offsets relative to each token, the operator enforces linear-combination regularization to preserve semantic consistency without requiring positional embeddings, maintaining strictly linear O(nT) compute and memory complexity.

Comprehensive empirical gains on predictive tasks: UPLiFT outperforms existing feature upsamplers across four semantic segmentation benchmarks (COCO-Stuff, Pascal VOC, ADE20K, Cityscapes) and achieves competitive depth estimation results on DINOv2 and DINOv3 backbones, while running noticeably faster (e.g., 79.4 ms vs. 111.7–223.5 ms) and consuming significantly less memory.

Insightful efficiency scaling analysis: Figures 1 and 9 provide compelling evidence showing that cross-attention baselines run out of memory around 1,500 visual tokens on 24 GB / 48 GB GPUs, whereas UPLiFT scales linearly and processes significantly higher token counts without OOM.

Novel extension to generative latent spaces: Extending feature upsampling to VAE latents for text-to-image and image super-resolution is an innovative direction, demonstrating strong speed-fidelity trade-offs compared to heavy iterative flow-matching methods (CFM).
weaknesses: Relation to prior dynamic local filtering / reassembly operators: The Local Attender is functionally very similar to existing content-aware reassembly operators such as CARAFE (Wang et al., ICCV 2019) and dynamic local convolutions. While CARAFE is cited, the paper lacks an explicit discussion or empirical comparison clarifying the differences and advantages of Local Attender over standard dynamic/bilateral reassembly kernels.

Performance gap on generative distribution metrics: In Table 4 (zero-shot super-resolution), although UPLiFT achieves higher SSIM/PSNR on LHQ, Coupled Flow Matching (CFM) substantially outperforms UPLiFT on distribution-level generative metrics (FacesHQ FID: 1.36 vs. 5.20; LHQ FID: 2.27 vs. 5.29). The paper should more transparently discuss this trade-off between deterministic reconstruction fidelity and distribution-level generation quality.

Bespoke heuristics required for generative tasks: Adapting UPLiFT to VAE latents necessitates several ad-hoc engineering additions (a post-attender Refiner Block, noise channel injection, and a test-time mean color correction heuristic) that are absent in the predictive setup. This reduces the conceptual generality and simplicity of the framework.

Architectural rigidity compared to continuous/arbitrary-scale upsamplers: Unlike coordinate-based or cross-attention approaches that can directly query arbitrary resolutions, UPLiFT is constrained to powers of two (requiring 16x upsampling followed by downsampling to handle 14x ViT patch strides).

strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem: existing state-of-the-art task-agnostic feature upsamplers (e.g., JAFAR, LoftUp, AnyUp) rely on global or windowed cross-attention that exhibits quadratic memory and time scaling, leading to out-of-memory (OOM) failures at high token counts.

The proposed Local Attender effectively resolves the semantic drift problem of prior iterative convolutional approaches (such as LiFT) while maintaining strict linear scaling O(nT) in computation and memory with token count, as convincingly verified in Figure 1 and Figure 9.

Comprehensive and strong empirical results on predictive benchmarks: UPLiFT consistently outperforms prior methods (FeatUp, LiFT, LoftUp, JAFAR, AnyUp) across semantic segmentation on four benchmarks (COCO, VOC, ADE20K, Cityscapes) and achieves competitive monocular depth estimation, all while requiring fewer parameters (0.8M) and faster inference (79.4 ms).

Effective expansion to generative tasks: the paper demonstrates the versatility of the method by applying it to VAE latent upsampling for text-to-image synthesis and super-resolution, matching or exceeding Coupled Flow Matching (CFM) with a fraction of parameters and inference cost.

Thorough ablations and qualitative validations, including detailed evaluations of training depth configurations, neighborhood size/patterns (Table 7), semantic stability PCA visualizations (Figure 10), and new foundation backbones like DINOv3.
weaknesses: Conceptual similarity to content-aware reassembly operators: The Local Attender operator bears strong algorithmic resemblance to existing dynamic local filtering operators, notably CARAFE (Wang et al., ICCV 2019), which also generates content-aware reassembly kernels via convolutional projection and softmax over a local neighborhood to pool features. The manuscript cites CARAFE in related works but lacks an explicit conceptual discussion and empirical comparison against it.

Architectural divergence between predictive and generative tasks: To work on VAE latents, UPLiFT requires several non-trivial modifications (scaling from 0.8M to 53.5M parameters, replacing BatchNorm with LayerNorm, adding noise injection, and introducing a post-attender Refiner Block). The Refiner Block relaxes the strict local convex combination constraint, indicating that the core Local Attender formulation alone is insufficient for generative synthesis.

Inherent resolution inflexibility of iterative 2x steps: Unlike continuous cross-attention approaches (JAFAR, LoftUp) that can directly query arbitrary continuous spatial coordinates, UPLiFT relies on discrete powers-of-two stages (e.g., performing 16x upsampling and downsampling back to 14x for patch-14 models), introducing minor computational redundancy.

strengths: Clear motivation and well-identified problem: Recent state-of-the-art feature upsamplers (e.g., JAFAR, LoftUp, AnyUp) rely on global or windowed cross-attention, causing quadratic scaling in latency and memory as token count increases. This paper convincingly revitalizes iterative feature upsampling while overcoming the semantic drift observed in earlier works like LiFT.

Well-designed and lightweight operator: The proposed Local Attender operates via localized attentional pooling across fixed directional offsets without positional encodings, guaranteeing linear $O(nT)$ time and memory scaling while preserving semantic consistency.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation across predictive tasks: Evaluated thoroughly across multiple benchmarks (COCO, VOC, ADE20K, Cityscapes) and depth estimation, demonstrating superior mIoU/accuracy over prior methods (LoftUp, JAFAR, AnyUp, LiFT, FeatUp) with substantially faster inference and lower memory usage. Tests with both DINOv2 and the recent DINOv3 confirm generalizability.

Novel application to generative tasks: Extending feature upsampling to VAE latent spaces for diffusion-based text-to-image synthesis and image super-resolution is an interesting and non-trivial direction. UPLiFT demonstrates competitive fidelity to iterative flow-matching methods (CFM) while requiring a fraction of the compute, training data, and inference time.

Thorough ablations: The supplementary material and ablation studies provide clear justifications for key design parameters, including training depth schedules, refiner blocks, and neighborhood structures.
weaknesses: Discussion of and comparison with related local reassembly operators: The Local Attender predicts attention/pooling weights from a guide feature over a fixed local neighborhood and resamples the value features. This shares significant conceptual similarity with Content-Aware ReAssembly of Features (CARAFE, Wang et al., ICCV 2019) and dynamic filtering networks. Although CARAFE is cited in Section 2, the paper lacks explicit architectural discussion and empirical comparison detailing the exact differences and advantages of Local Attender over standard content-aware reassembly modules.

Gap on generative distribution metrics: In the super-resolution evaluation (Table 4), while UPLiFT achieves competitive PSNR/SSIM and is much faster, CFM achieves markedly better perceptual distribution scores (FID of 1.36 vs 5.20 on FacesHQ, and 2.27 vs 5.29 on LHQ). A brief discussion regarding why regression-based iterative upsampling struggles slightly on distribution metrics compared to generative flow matching would provide better context.

Multi-scale training overhead: The training objective (Section 3.3) requires computing ground-truth features at multiple downsampled resolutions by feeding downscaled images through the frozen visual backbone. While training is only for one epoch on ImageNet-1K, the paper should clearly report the training time and GPU memory requirements compared to single-scale training baselines.
